objective: Fix Issue #183 within Backend only: reject non-finite numbers before local JSONL caching and remote JSON projection, and prevent generated HTTP JSON responses from reporting success when serialization fails. Use main commit e77ac35212b73838b2bbc47b28182ca06c18cf0d as the fixed implementation and boundary baseline.
decision_supported: Can Backend keep invalid numeric evidence out of trusted reads and return truthful, bounded HTTP failures without changing shared contracts or other modules?
outputs: The five allowed files only; create new regression classes BackendStrictJsonReadModelTests and BackendStrictJsonResponseTests in test_dashboard_backend.py, and RemoteStrictJsonTests in test_multi_host.py.

Red/green command output, collected test node IDs, real loopback HTTP evidence, and fixed-base boundary results. Keep transient logs outside the repository; do not commit, push, create a PR, or mark the Issue complete.
acceptance: T01 (test_finite_controls in BackendStrictJsonReadModelTests and RemoteStrictJsonTests): BackendStrictJsonReadModelTests and RemoteStrictJsonTests preserve valid finite inputs including 0, -0.0, 1e308, 1e-300, integers, booleans, null, Unicode strings, nested objects/arrays, and the literal strings NaN/Infinity. No extra domain range or precision policy is introduced.

T02 (BackendStrictJsonReadModelTests.test_local_nonfinite_matrix): BackendStrictJsonReadModelTests reject NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, 1e400 and -1e400 in top-level object members and nested objects/arrays, including unused fields and later JSONL records, through ReadModelError before invalid data is cached or summarized. Local and remote decoding reuse the same Backend-private rule and retain duplicate-key rejection.

T03 (BackendStrictJsonReadModelTests.test_cache_recovers_after_nonfinite_change): BackendStrictJsonReadModelTests prove valid-to-invalid-to-valid file changes fail closed and recover under the existing path/mtime_ns/size cache policy. Invalid new content never replaces a valid cache entry and is never hidden by stale successful reads; unchanged valid cache reuse remains intact. Use explicit file metadata/size changes, never sleep.

T04 (BackendStrictJsonResponseTests.test_local_http_fails_closed): BackendStrictJsonResponseTests use real loopback HTTP to prove a malformed local numeric source yields 503 with status=not_ready at /readyz and 503 invalid_event_source on run-list, run-detail and event routes, including /api and /api/v1 aliases. /healthz remains 200 and invalid sources produce no partial successful run list.

T05 (RemoteStrictJsonTests.test_remote_nonfinite_matrix): RemoteStrictJsonTests exercise actual RemoteDashboardReadModel decoding and a real loopback upstream/controller boundary. Invalid numeric /readyz response bodies yield false readiness and controller 503; invalid run-list and event bodies yield ReadModelError and controller 503 invalid_event_source. Valid responses preserve behavior. No new cross-endpoint readiness probing or sticky health state is added.

T06 (BackendStrictJsonResponseTests.test_serialization_failure_before_headers): BackendStrictJsonResponseTests prove all JSON responses generated by server.py use allow_nan=False or an equivalent strict encoding path, including normal, overload and error responses. Inject nested Python NaN/positive infinity/negative infinity and ordinary TypeError/ValueError/UnicodeError serialization failures; choose a bounded 503 response_serialization_failed JSON error before writing any success status, headers or body. The fallback is fixed and nonrecursive.

T07 (test_error_redaction_and_headers in BackendStrictJsonResponseTests and RemoteStrictJsonTests): BackendStrictJsonResponseTests and RemoteStrictJsonTests assert new numeric/serialization failure messages and captured logs do not contain source payloads, remote response bodies, sensitive sentinel values or attacker-controlled field names. Preserve Content-Type, accurate byte Content-Length, existing security headers and any API-version header already supplied to the response function.

T08 (BackendStrictJsonResponseTests.test_strict_json_oracle plus all response assertions): Positive and negative response tests validate actual response bytes with an independent strict JSON oracle that rejects constants and decoded non-finite floats. A test verifies the oracle rejects all five invalid-number cases. JSON Schema validation or default json.loads alone is not sufficient evidence.

T09: Both existing test files pass without relaxing duplicate-key, normal split-host, 404, 405 read-only, 403 peer rejection, exact 4 MiB/4 MiB+1 response-size, 16-request concurrency, timeout, redirect or allow-list tests. Preserve existing interfaces, OpenAPI, event semantics and all limits.

T10: Add the three named test classes before implementation and run each separately. Record expected assertion failures for the missing numeric/HTTP safeguards, then green results for the same node IDs. Collection/import errors, missing dependencies, skipped tests or zero collected tests are not red/green evidence. All Packet commands and make check must pass before handoff.
evidence: Record the actual WSL worktree, branch, HEAD, clean/dirty status, Python version and imported workbench_backend.__file__. The Windows checkout E:/Projects/workbench-desk-robot is classification-only and must not be modified.

T01-T03: collected test node IDs and before/after outputs for valid numeric controls, all five invalid tokens, nested/unused members, later invalid JSONL records, and deterministic cache invalidation/recovery.

T04-T07: actual loopback HTTP status, headers and bounded response bytes; no-success-before-serialization evidence; captured-log and error redaction assertions. Any mocked input or injected encoder failure must be identified explicitly.
T08-T09: strict-oracle self-test and existing Backend/multi-host regression results, including response-size and network-boundary controls.

T10: three implementation-before red runs and their matching green runs, focused regression output, make check results and every command exit code. Do not report earlier 45-test baseline success as evidence that new behavior is implemented.

Packet validation against the fixed base e77ac35212b73838b2bbc47b28182ca06c18cf0d plus staged/unstaged/untracked path inspection. Plain git diff does not include untracked files and is not sufficient boundary evidence.
stop_conditions: Stop before implementation unless the human Owner has approved this Packet and a separate Issue #183 worktree starts from fixed main base e77ac35212b73838b2bbc47b28182ca06c18cf0d. Do not implement on Issue #47 or #62 branches or silently change the baseline.
Stop if any source, test or documentation change outside allowed_paths is required; preserve all existing user changes and do not alter the Packet scope without explicit approval.

Stop for any required change to interfaces, shared contracts/OpenAPI, multiple modules, robot/control, firmware or safety configuration; obtain the corresponding human Owner approvals before revising scope.

Stop if the work requires Issue #65 full event semantic validation, cross-endpoint readiness aggregation, WorldState mutation, producer migration, a new JSON dependency, a generalized validator or arbitrary-precision number policy.
Stop if existing cache identity/immutability, deployment trust, authentication, redirects, concurrency, timeout or response-size policy must be redesigned or weakened.

Stop if baseline import paths point to another worktree, required fixtures/dependencies are missing, tests collect zero or are skipped, or expected red assertions cannot be reproduced; resolve prerequisites without editing unrelated files.
Stop if Packet validation encounters symbolic-link boundaries or unrelated Git changes; report the exact cause rather than weakening forbidden rules or moving/removing user environments.
Stop if an out-of-scope baseline or make check failure requires unrelated code/config changes. No commit, push, PR creation, deletion or rewrite of historical event evidence is authorized.
data_classification: Public source code and synthetic local fixtures only; no credentials, private run logs or real sensor payloads.
model_policy: Use local deterministic tests and synthetic loopback HTTP peers; do not contact production event sources or claim physical/safety validation.
risks_and_fallbacks: Historical non-finite logs will fail closed. Retain them unchanged and identify the producer; no automatic data migration or value substitution.
1e400 is valid JSON number syntax but overflows the existing Python float representation. Reject the resulting non-finite value without claiming support for arbitrary precision.
Remote readiness checks only its own response body in this slice; valid readiness paired with independently malformed remote event content is not solved by a new polling/health mechanism here.

Changes to invalid-input responses are externally observable. Request Backend and affected Dashboard/API consumer review at PR time without claiming that a passing schema or AI review is human approval.
Existing OpenAPI omissions, including the run-detail route's already-implemented 503 behavior, are not repaired here. If acceptance needs a public contract amendment, stop for Owner review.
